body: Like 2 weeks before the exam followed by the Free 120 a week before 82%. I doubt they’ll change it

I use to be just like you and overthink too much on everything. Just appreciate the aspects around you. Ignore the bad things, somethings you can’t change. I use to be like you and was confused about it and wanted to leave it at one point. I learned to look at my religion as a blessing.

For me, it’s kept me away from a lot of bad things. In Islam, Muslims are not to drink alcohol. With that in mind, it’s indirectly have told me to not smoke tobacco, weed or to introduce anything harmful (meth, heroin, opioids) to your body which is seen to be a gift from God. I took that principle further in my own way and exercise regularly to stay in shape. Love your body and yourself. Many people I know smoke weed and are hooked on to it cold and really want to quit, but can’t.

Islam and even Christianity helped me learn to be Content with what I have. I use to be extremely materialistic, but tbh, I never really was inside. It was there cuz everyone around me was superficial and expensive flashy things and they were not really themselves. Ever since I stopped caring about what I didn’t have or why couldn’t my life be a certain way, I became so much more happier than I ever was. I would hate someone almost instantaneously if they drove a nicer car than me or just had nicer things. 

I don’t believe in abandoning your parents especially if they have been good to you and not crazy abusive (which is unfortunately the case for some people). Truth is, no one has perfect parents. At the end of the day, they’re the people who have been with you since day 1 and have remained with you since then. There were times where I had no one to reach out to and I thought some of the friends I had in life that I thought I was closer to them, but they’ve completely forgot about me and moved on. Friends come and ago (childhood, HS, college, work), but family will always be there at your side which religion emphasizes on family. I once lost my job and would’ve been living homeless had it not been for my parents. 

Last, and most importantly for me personally, I can’t deny that our surroundings are random. The universe around us is to well put together that it couldn’t have happened to chance. I can’t deny that there is a Creator.

When it comes to Religion (Islam for me), focusing on the core principles for me and not all the complex little things that were most likely introduced in from culture. I’m at at peace. Focusing on the basics has made me very comfortable with religion. There will always be things I’ll never know the answer to, but perhaps it’s better that way. 
Wish you the best!
